That German wording is NOT in the deposit and NOT in either supplement (s001.docx is the PPOS-D6 German/English appendix, s002.docx is the PPOS correlation table; neither mentions coercion), and it is the authors' own ad hoc translation, so Efkemann et al.'s separately published German SACS is not a substitute for it. The paper's direction inverts all three into readings no first-semester medical-student sample would produce. The shipped anchors follow the codebook. Two obvious misspellings in the RESPONSE ANCHORS were corrected and are named here: 'rahter agrre' -> 'rather agree' (resp 3), and trailing spaces stripped from 'agree ' and 'disagree '. ITEM WORDING was NOT touched, so three source typos ship verbatim: item 8 'Coercion violates the patients integrity.' (no apostrophe), item 13 'To much coercion is used in treatment.' ('To' for 'Too'), item 7 has no closing period. The instruction text likewise ships with its lower-case opening ('coercive measures in medicine are a special challenge...') exactly as the codebook has it. That is a property of the responses, not a gap in the option set; audit_batch.R may flag it. RIGHTS: extracted, not blocked. The instrument is the SACS (Husum, Finset & Ruud, 2008, Int J Law Psychiatry 31:417-422). No clause reserving a right could be found or quoted anywhere on the rights holder's side. Searched: the two Husum-authored SACS reviews (Front Psychiatry 2022;13:744661 PMC9095955 and 2023;14:1063276 PMC9941667, both CC BY, both by the scale's own developers) -- neither states any term of use, neither reprints the items, and the only permission-adjacent sentence in either is a description of their own literature-search method ('researchers who have asked for permission to use the scale since its development in 2008 were contacted and asked for their possible results'), which records what some users did, not a requirement addressed to users. Husum maintains no rights or measures-library page that could be fetched. Per the 2026-09-05/2026-09-08 rulings, silence is permission and a block with no quote in it is not a block, so this ships. Its value labels carry the anchors, identical for all three items: 1 Completely disagree / 2 Disagree / 3 Neither disagree nor agree / 4 Agree / 5 Completely agree -- the same map the processing script's LIKERT5 dict applies, so the resp axis is label-tied at the source too, not inferred. (2) STEP 3b: instrument confirmed against the paper's Methods -- 'A three-item scale of natural immunity beliefs was taken from the Martin and Petrie [41], Vaccination Attitudes Examination (VAX) scale. Those items were answered on a five-point scale ranging from 1 = completely disagree to 5 = completely agree'. Live data agrees: 3 items, resp 1-5, n=577 per item. The three .sav labels are character-for-character the VAX scale's own published natural-immunity items as printed in Martin & Petrie (2017) Table 2 (Auckland-hosted PDF), differing only in that the deposit drops the terminal full stop on each; the labels are shipped verbatim as read, so no period was added. (3) STORED DIRECTION CHECKED, not assumed: summing the three raw .sav columns gives M=6.60, SD=3.63 over n=577, reproducing the paper's published subscale total (M = 6.60, SD = 3.63) exactly, so the table stores the items raw and in the scored direction (higher = stronger natural-immunity preference). No reverse-keyed items in this subscale. (4) LANGUAGE: administered in Croatian. The paper states 'All the instruments were translated into Croatian, and then back-translated in order to check the validity of the translation.' Neither the article nor its supplements publishes any Croatian wording -- the S1 .sav is the only supplement carrying item text and every label in it is English (zero Croatian item strings; the only Croatian in the file is the derived variable name 'Spol_pismenost_interakcija'). So the translated_substitute fallback applies: the study's own English sits in the base fields, language=Croatian, no _translated columns emitted. translation_source=study_supplied (the deposit's variable labels), which here is also verbatim the instrument publisher's English. (5) STRUCTURE: instructions and section_prompt are NA -- neither the paper nor the deposit publishes any prompt or instruction text for this block, only the 1-5 anchor description already carried by option_text; nothing was invented to fill them. Single trivial section_id; correct_response NA (attitude scale, no key). (6) RIGHTS: no block. The VAX scale is not in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. Martin & Petrie (2017) 'Understanding the Dimensions of Anti-Vaccination Attitudes: the Vaccination Attitudes Examination (VAX) Scale', Ann Behav Med 51(5):652-660, doi:10.1007/s12160-017-9888-y, prints all 12 items in its Table 2 and carries only a bare copyright line, '# The Society of Behavioral Medicine 2017' -- a notice about the article, not a term governing the instrument (the PANAS case). The authors' own lab hosts the full article PDF openly at https://www.fmhs.auckland.ac.nz/assets/fmhs/som/psychmed/petrie/docs/2017%20Vax%20Scale.pdf (fetched 2026-09-09), and it carries no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause; no rights page for the VAX scale is locatable. Silence is permission, so extracted normally -- nothing quotable to record. The wording additionally sits in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE deposit, though that governs the response data rather than the instrument. (7) A BLOCK WOULD HAVE ACHIEVED LITTLE ANYWAY (irw#2101 shape): the item codes Imm1..Imm3 carry no wording, but the deposit that produced the table is the public PLOS supplement whose variable labels hold the items.
